author: thomas_hardy
text: When we go on our journey through life, we carry some things with us as if we were going home to die; we don't know whether it will be home or death that awaits us on the other side. We take along with us everything from childhood; we keep all our clothes, because these have become part of us and give evidence of what has happened between them and us. The day before the funeral service was held at the grave of one of my old friends who had died suddenly. He had been a good man and he was much loved by everyone in the community where he lived.

author: sara_teasdale
text:
Happy!

We have a little boy; his name is Richard.
And we have another who will be born in May.
They’ll make us happier than we ever were before.
If you could know how much I love my dear old husband,
You would understand why I say that every day,
“Happiness is here.”

author: stephen_crane
text:
VI

God's foot was on the ladder-top;
He felt his way, as blinde men do--
Feeling their path with their fingertips.
First one step, and then another;
And when it seemed as if he stood
Within that dark unknowable wood
Of futurity, there came at last
The touch of solid ground!

author: thomas_hardy
text:
In this world we are all as poor as Lazarus
Who stood at Abraham's gate to-night,
And saw his Master pass on by,
Too far away to hear him call;
Too slow, too weak, too dull to fly!

But when he turned again in haste
To look upon his face one more time,
The bread had left its place
On Christ's fair brow, where it was once
So freshly set,--and now seemed dry,
While His great hands were empty of food.

We know that in a house of dust there is nothing left behind;
And all those men who are born on this earth go by.
But God hath other secrets which He keeps within Him
From us who come to him as from him we have gone.

author: sara_teasdale
text:
_The old brown horse snorted as he trod over a brook in the road. He was tied to
a tree beside it; but it was an afternoon when horses were restless all along the
road from Worcester. His rider came round at last, his mind still on his business
and not on the horse. The horse snort again, shook himself like a terrier. He had
been out most of the day with a heavy wagon full of wood, and had gone through
many rough places which had made him more restive than ever._
